text:
Tripo P2.0 updates low-poly modeling with AI

Good Sunday morning, tech enthusiasts! Today’s news is all about a significant update from Tripo Studio that could shake up the world of low-poly and mid-poly asset creation for games and other applications. Are you ready to dive into some serious 3D modeling improvements? Let's see what this new version brings.
What’s New in Tripo P2.0?

The big news here is the introduction of native quad topology, which means models are now generated with a 4-sided mesh structure right out of the gate. This isn’t just about aesthetics; it’s about functionality. The new architecture ensures that edges flow correctly and anatomical loops around joints, eyes, and mouths are properly set up for rigging and skinning.

Another key feature is Smart UV, an AI-driven tool that automatically unwraps 13D models into a flat layout for texturing. This process used to be tedious and time-consuming but now happens in mere seconds thanks to Tripo’s Spatial Diffusion architecture. The system intelligently places seams based on anatomical understanding and geometry, hiding them where they won’t be noticeable.
Why Should You Care?

For 3D artists and game developers working with low-poly assets, this is a huge step forward. Low-poly models are essential for real-time rendering in games and VR applications due to their performance benefits. However, creating these models manually can be incredibly labor-intensive. Tripo P2.0 aims to streamline the entire process from concept to final export.

The ability to generate clean topology with correct edge flow means that your models will be ready for rigging right out of the box. This saves a ton of time and effort in post-processing, allowing you to focus more on creative aspects rather than technical minutiae.
How Does It Work?

Tripo P2.0 uses an architecture called Spatial Diffusion to rapidly generate base 3D forms within seconds. Once this initial form is established, the system refines it with textures and lighting over a period of about two to three minutes. This process includes removing baked-in lighting from textures so that colors are neutral and correctly displayed in engines like Unity or Unreal.

The Smart UV feature takes things even further by automatically unwrapping your model’s mesh into a 2D layout for texturing. It places seams intelligently based on the object's anatomy, ensuring they’re hidden where possible. This is particularly useful when dealing with complex characters and props that would normally require intricate manual work.
What Is Stored?

When you use Tripo P2.0 to generate models, your input data (like images or sketches) and the resulting 3D model files are stored on their servers temporarily for processing. Once the job is complete, these files can be downloaded directly from the platform. However, Tripo does not retain any personal information beyond what’s necessary for account management.
What Is Excluded?

While Tripo P2.0 excels at generating low-poly models and handling UV unwrapping, it doesn’t cover high-detail sculpting or advanced texturing techniques that require manual intervention. Additionally, the platform focuses on 3D modeling rather than animation or rigging beyond initial setup.
User Controls

Users have control over their generated assets through various settings within Tripo P2.0. You can adjust parameters like polygon count and texture resolution to fine-tune your models before downloading them. The free tier allows you to generate two models without any subscription, while paid plans offer more features and higher limits.
Availability

Tripo Studio’s official site is where you can access the latest version of Tripo P2.0. The platform supports up to 80,000 triangles or 40,000 quads for Smart UV processing, which should cover most low-poly needs. Additionally, Tripo offers a generous free tier where users can generate two models without any subscription. Beyond that, the cost is 20 credits per model, with three free retries included on Pro/Max/Team plans.
What This Does Not Prove

While Tripo P2.0 significantly simplifies low-poly modeling and UV unwrapping, it doesn’t prove that AI can replace human creativity entirely. The platform still relies heavily on user input for initial concepts and design direction. Moreover, the quality of the final product depends on how well you understand and utilize these tools.
Practical Takeaway

If you’re a 3D artist or game developer looking to streamline your workflow, Tripo P2.0 offers a compelling solution with its native quad topology and Smart UV features. The free tier is a great place to start experimenting without breaking the bank. Give it a try and see how it fits into your creative process.

What changes for you? Will this make your 3D modeling workflow more efficient? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

So, guys, have you ever wondered how brands are finding the right people to work on cutting-edge AI projects? And have you thought about showcasing your own expertise in these technologies? Well, Runway has just launched DIFFUSE, a platform designed specifically for that purpose. But is it really as straightforward as it sounds?
How It Works

DIFFUSE operates like a specialized version of Behance and LinkedIn, but with a focus on AI-native creatives. You can build your profile, showcase your portfolio, and connect directly with potential clients who are looking for specific skills in AI-driven content creation. The platform doesn’t handle payment or provide guarantees; it’s purely a matchmaking service.
What’s Actually New?

The novelty here is that DIFFUSE addresses the growing demand for creative professionals skilled in using cutting-edge AI tools like Runway, Midjourney, Seedance, Nano Banana, ElevenLabs, and Suno. While similar platforms exist, DIFFUSE caters specifically to this niche market, making it easier for both job seekers and employers to find each other.
Why Should You Care?

If you’re part of the creative industry, whether as an independent artist or a brand looking for innovative content creation, DIFFUSE could be your new go-to resource. It’s designed to cater to the specific needs of this evolving field, making it easier to connect with talent that can bring AI-driven creativity to life.
The Dark Side

But here’s where things get tricky: Runway isn’t taking any responsibility for transactions or outcomes on DIFFUSE. This means there are no guarantees about project completion, quality control, or even basic protections like escrow services. Essentially, you’re on your own when it comes to negotiating terms and ensuring that projects meet expectations.
What’s Stored

On DIFFUSE, users can store their profiles, portfolios, and connections. The platform allows for detailed customization of these elements, giving creatives a robust space to showcase their work and expertise. However, the data stored is limited to what you upload or create within the platform itself.
What’s Excluded

Runway isn’t acting as an employment agency; they’re just providing a platform for direct connections. This means there are no official job listings or guaranteed placements through the service. Additionally, DIFFUSE doesn’t handle payment transactions, so users must manage these aspects independently.
User Controls

When it comes to sensitive topics like intellectual property rights, Runway doesn’t provide default protections on DIFFUSE. Users must opt-in to any additional services or agreements separately if they want extra safeguards. This gives you control over your profile and portfolio files, allowing you to edit or delete content as needed without worrying about permanent records.
Availability

DIFFUSE is currently available as an open platform, and while there are no specific limitations mentioned, users should be aware that the service operates without guarantees. It’s also worth checking if your preferred plan includes access to DIFFUSE features, especially if you’re a Runway enterprise customer.
What This Does Not Prove

It's worth noting that DIFFUSE doesn't prove Runway is taking over the creative industry or replacing human talent entirely. The platform simply provides a space for those who want to work with AI tools to connect more easily, but it doesn’t guarantee employment or project success.
Practical Takeaway

DIFFUSE is an interesting move by Runway to tap into the growing market of AI-native creatives. While it offers valuable connections, it also leaves users navigating a largely unregulated space with significant risks involved. So, if you’re jumping in, make sure you know what you’re getting into and have your legal ducks in a row.
Live Updates vs Old Summaries

DIFFUSE is a new platform, so there are no old summaries to compare against. However, as it evolves, users can expect live updates and changes that reflect the growing demand for AI-native talent in the creative industry.

text:
Google launches Gemini 3.8 TTS for voice cloning

8 TTS (Text-to-Speech). This isn’t just another update; it’s a significant move in the world of voice synthesis and automation.
What Is Gemini 3.8 TTS?

Gemini 3.8 TTS comes in two flavors: Gemini 7.8 Flash TTS for creative work and character voices, and Gemini 7.8 Flash-Lite TTS for large-scale projects where cost efficiency is crucial. The model boasts an impressive array of features designed to enhance voice generation across multiple languages and dialects.
Voice Generation Across Languages

One of the standout features of Gemini 3.8 TTS is its ability to generate voices from text descriptions in over 100 languages and dialects, including regional variations like Mexican Spanish, Quebecois French, and Scottish English. This versatility opens up new possibilities for content creators who need localized voiceovers.
Cloning Voices with SynthID

Another exciting feature is the capability to clone a voice from just a 30-second sample. The model even includes SynthID watermarks for verification purposes, ensuring that cloned voices are authentic and traceable. This could be a game-changer for those looking to replicate specific vocal styles or personalities.
Handling Direction with Ease

Gemini 3.8 TTS excels in handling direction through plain language stage directions embedded directly into scripts. The model can accurately interpret these cues, maintaining voice stability over long audio sessions and supporting natural dialogues between multiple speakers. It even nails non-verbal sounds like laughs, sighs, and interruptions.
Benchmarks and Performance

According to benchmarks from Hume AI Voice Design and Voice Arena, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS leads in several categories:
• Hume AI Voice Design: Score of 71.4
• Accent Accuracy: Score of 60.8
• Voice Arena: Top rankings for Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, Vietnamese, Arabic, Mexican Spanish, and Hindi

These scores reflect the model’s ability to replicate real human voice characteristics accurately across various languages and scenarios.
Real-World Performance Considerations

While these benchmarks are impressive, it's important to note that they represent ideal conditions. In practice, performance may vary based on input quality and context. For instance, noisy environments or poorly recorded samples might affect the model’s output accuracy.
Legal Hurdles in Voice Cloning

Despite its potential, Gemini 3.8 TTS faces significant legal challenges in certain regions due to privacy concerns and data protection laws. Voice cloning is not available in the EU, UK, Switzerland, India, Illinois, and Texas. This limitation underscores the importance of compliance with local regulations when deploying such technologies.
Under-the-Hood Technology

Gemini 3.8 TTS leverages advanced neural networks trained on vast datasets of human voices speaking various languages and dialects. This training allows the model to mimic accents and inflections with remarkable accuracy, making it a powerful tool for content creators and voice artists alike.
Cost Efficiency with Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite

For those working on large-scale projects where cost is a concern, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS offers an efficient solution. While it may not match the full capabilities of its counterpart, it provides a balance between performance and budget constraints.
Competition in Text-to-Speech Models

As Google rolls out Gemini 3.8 TTS, other tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft are likely to respond with their own advancements in text-to-speech technology. The race for perfect natural voice synthesis is far from over, and the competition will undoubtedly drive further innovation in this space.
What This Does Not Prove

It’s crucial to remember that while Gemini 3.8 TTS excels in certain areas, it doesn’t prove that AI can replace human creativity entirely. There are still nuances in human expression that machines struggle with, such as emotional depth and spontaneous improvisation.
Practical Takeaway

So, what’s your take? Are you excited about the possibilities offered by Gemini 3.8 TTS, or do you have reservations due to its limitations? Do you think it raises more questions than it answers?

text:
LOOK UP THE PRICE OF OIL THIS WEEKEND AND YOU GET TWO ANSWERS, $6.88 APART:

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has two honest prices right now. Brent for November delivery ended Friday at $104.32 a barrel, -$2.28 / -2.14%. Brent for December delivery ended at $97.44, -$2.78 / -2.77%. Some quote pages already show December as "Brent"; others still show November. The November contract stops trading Wednesday, September 30. After that every page shows December - an apparent drop of about $6.88, or 6.6%, without a single barrel getting cheaper.

The verdict: the gap is the news, not the switch. Buyers are paying $6.88 more to get oil one month sooner, the widest gap between these two months all year. That says the shortage is now, and it is where President Trump's Saturday rejection of Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz lands first.

Europe, East Asia and New York have not traded since Friday, so every level below is a last close.

Europe finished Friday quiet: FTSE 100 (UK) at 10,695.25, +15.26 pts / +0.14%; DAX (Germany) at 25,408.64, +142.11 pts / +0.56%; CAC 40 (France) at 8,077.80, -3.63 pts / -0.04%. The London price that matters most this week is not a stock index. Brent trades on ICE Futures Europe, a London exchange, and reopens Sunday at 11pm London time, 6pm ET.

Asia closed before Europe opened. Nikkei 225 (Japan) at 66,364.20, +850.21 pts / +1.30% in Friday's session, a fifth straight gain, helped partly by oil sliding on hopes of a Hormuz deal. Hang Seng (Hong Kong) at 24,510.09, -251.04 pts / -1.01% on Friday. Shanghai Composite at 3,888.37, -48.15 pts / -1.22% in Thursday's session; mainland China was shut Friday for a holiday. Tokyo reopens at 8pm ET tonight, Hong Kong and Shanghai at 9:30pm ET.

How to read the gap. A futures contract is an agreement made today on the price of oil delivered in a set month. In a calm market, next month's oil costs about the same as this month's, or a little more, because someone has to store it. When the nearer month costs far more, buyers are paying extra to get barrels sooner - the market's way of saying oil is scarce now and expected to be less scarce later.

November minus December, through 2026:
- February 27, the last trading day before the war began: 45 cents
- April 30: $2.52
- Early July, with November Brent near $72: briefly below zero, meaning December cost slightly more
- July 23: $3.01, the widest before September
- September 15: $5.44
- Friday: $6.88 - Thursday and Friday are the only two days of 2026 above $6

Friday had a wrinkle. Both months fell on deal hopes, but December fell more, so the gap widened on a down day.

Further out, the discount keeps growing. Brent for October 2027 delivery ended Friday at $81.66, $22.66 under November. Traders are paying for a shortage now and pricing a much smaller one a year from now.

Why Saturday hits the near month hardest. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, offered to reopen the strait within seven days if the US lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports and waived sanctions on Iranian oil. President Trump called it "not acceptable." On Sunday, Araghchi said Tehran had seen those remarks but had received no official US reply through the mediators. A strait reopened within a week would have eased the soonest barrels first - exactly the months carrying the premium.

America's own oil tells the same story at half the volume. West Texas Intermediate, the US benchmark, ended Friday at $92.44 for November, -$2.17 / -2.29%, and $88.84 for December: a $3.60 gap, about half of Brent's. Oil pumped in Texas does not have to cross an ocean; Brent is the price for oil that does, competing for the same buyers as the cargoes stuck behind Hormuz. WTI's November contract expires October 20, so US quote pages face the same switch three weeks later.

For New York, oil is the line to interest rates. Fuel costs feed inflation, and the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16, its first increase since 2023, as the war's energy shock pushed prices up.

US stock futures ended Friday higher and have not traded since; each move runs from Thursday's close:
- S&P 500 futures at 7,803.75, +36.75 pts / +0.47%
- Nasdaq-100 futures at 30,889.25, +122.50 pts / +0.40%
- Dow futures at 52,163, +446 pts / +0.86%
- Russell 2000 futures at 2,859.30, +2.50 pts / +0.09%

They reopen at 6pm ET tonight, the same minute as oil, and moves made while New York sleeps can fade by Monday's 9:30am ET open.

What would change the verdict: the November-December gap shrinking well below $6.88 before Wednesday, with the strait still shut, would say buyers see more oil arriving sooner - real relief. A gap wider than $6.88 when trading reopens tonight says Saturday's no is being priced where it bites. The risk is Thursday's quote page showing Brent near $7 lower, and readers taking it for the war easing.

Wednesday retires the expensive month from the headlines. It does not retire the shortage that made it expensive.

Not investment advice.

text:
Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington (September 23–25) offers a useful comparative case: how the same three days get processed very differently depending on both sides.

- On the US side, the framing splits along institutional and ideological lines rather than presenting a single line. Official readouts and outlets like CNN and NPR describe a summit "heavy on optics and symbolism, light on substantive progress," with both leaders essentially convinced that only they can manage the other. CSIS frames it as an exercise in stabilising the relationship rather than resolving it, useful precisely because it locks in a pattern of regular high-level contact.

- The concrete deliverables reported on the US side are narrow and transactional: a fentanyl tariff reduction, a one-year reprieve on rare-earth export curbs, movement on the TikTok divestiture arrangement, and continuation of the "trade truce" first struck at Busan. Taiwan, notably, was reported as absent from Trump's own public readout, even as it remained a live undercurrent elsewhere in the coverage.

- More hawkish US commentary, Fox News being the clearest example, reads the same visit almost adversarially: Xi's conciliatory tone is interpreted as tactical rather than genuine, tied to domestic Communist Party pressures, and the entire "strategic stability" formulation is treated with open suspicion as cover for continued fentanyl flows, IP practices and support for Russia. This is a minority framing but not a marginal one, and it signals that any durable improvement in ties will face resistance from parts of the US policy and media establishment regardless of what is signed in Washington.

- On the Chinese side, Xinhua and CCTV coverage is considerably more uniform, which is expected given the state-media structure, but the consistency itself is analytically informative. Both outlets centre the phrase "constructive relationship of strategic stability" almost verbatim across reports, describing the visit as providing "new strategic guidance" for the bilateral relationship. This reflects a deliberate effort to institutionalise a specific diplomatic vocabulary as the accepted frame for the relationship going forward, in the same way "peaceful rise" or "win-win cooperation" functioned in earlier periods.

- Wang Yi's post-visit statement, carried by Xinhua, describes the trip as having "maintained the overall stability of Sino-US relations" and lists outcomes such as a new communication channel on advanced AI, positioning Beijing as a stabilising, cooperative actor rather than a reactive one. The emphasis throughout is on reciprocity, parity and the idea of two major powers meeting as equals, reinforced by the fact that this was Xi's first visit to Washington in over a decade and is being read domestically as restored standing rather than routine diplomacy.

- At the same time, Chinese messaging was not purely conciliatory. A parallel piece attributed to Ambassador Xie Feng in the People's Daily lays out four explicit red lines: Taiwan, democracy and human rights, development path, and development rights, stating plainly that these "cannot be challenged." This is worth noting because it shows Beijing pairing the soft language of "strategic stability" with a hard restatement of non-negotiables aimed at its own domestic audience as much as at Washington, a pattern consistent with how Chinese diplomacy typically manages simultaneous signalling to two audiences.

- US coverage largely treats the summit as a transactional event to be measured against specific line items: tariffs, rare earths, TikTok, fentanyl enforcement. Chinese state media treats it as a legitimising event, less about individual deliverables and more about normalising a bilateral framework in which China is positioned as co-equal manager of the relationship rather than a subordinate or disruptive actor.

text:
IRAN MINES HORMUZ AFTER TRUMP SAID NO: LARGEST NIGHT ATTACK OF THE WAR

Overnight the Strait of Hormuz stopped looking like a contested shipping lane and started looking like a battlefield. Reports from the Gulf describe the heaviest Iranian attack since the war began — anti-ship missiles, speedboats, and mines laid across the routes tankers still use. Oil desks opened talking $200. What changed is not one hit. It is who now claims the water itself.

THE NIGHT STRIKE
➡️ Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces launched what reports call the largest attack on the strait since the war started.
➡️ Anti-ship missiles and cruise missiles were fired along the southern route.
➡️ At the same time, sea mines were laid on commercial lanes — including the Omani corridor ships had used to slip around earlier minefields.
➡️ Some of the cruise missiles were reported to be carrying mines.

THE TANKERS
➡️ Residents in the northern United Arab Emirates described dozens of loud explosions.
➡️ Several ships were reported hit. Exact numbers remain unconfirmed.
➡️ At least three vessels were described as heavily damaged. A fourth turned around. One source put the night’s tally as high as six large ships.
➡️ Guard speedboats operated around Larak island and were said to have fired guided missiles, machine guns, and small arms at tankers.
➡️ Further explosions were reported off Sirik, with a sea clash near Qeshm.

THE TIMING
➡️ The mining began hours after Donald Trump rejected Iran’s offer to reopen the strait.
➡️ A new Guard warning went out to any ship that tries to ignore Tehran’s rules.
➡️ Pre-war traffic was dozens of ships a day, sometimes more than 140.
➡️ The Guard spokesman now says the oil that still moves is partner crude with Tehran’s permission. Ships outside that system, he said, can be counted on one hand.
➡️ When vessels abort, reroute, or simply stay away, the fight is no longer just about individual tankers. It is about the traffic lane.
➡️ Washington still describes the strait as open. Iran´s  answer is that this story exists to cap the oil price — and that they intend to stop it.

THE SEVEN CONDITIONS
➡️ Guard spokesman Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi said Iran will keep punishing the United States until seven conditions are met.
➡️ Those conditions were already rejected at the UN General Assembly.
➡️ “We will not stop punishing the United States until they fulfill Iran’s seven conditions.”
➡️ He called Iran the victor of the war and said the fight is being turned into lasting strategic deterrence.
➡️ He also said the world’s largest navy could not keep Hormuz open even for a few hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
The waterway that feeds the world’s energy trade is being treated as a weapon: missiles first, mines second, permits third. Trump can meet the seven points or try to blast the lane back open. What he cannot do is leave the map as it was last night.
The barrel is now priced off a mined strait, not a speech.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has offered Washington a proposed seven-day roadmap aimed at restoring normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and restarting nuclear negotiations.

Under the reported proposal, the U.S. would first take steps including easing the naval blockade, providing sanctions relief and releasing around $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets, alongside a wider regional ceasefire.

If the conditions were implemented, Iran would then restore normal maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz around the sixth day, with U.S.-Iran nuclear negotiations resuming on the seventh day.

But U.S. President Donald Trump has publicly rejected the proposal, saying he “reject[ed] their proposal” and “rejected their deal.”

There is, however, an important diplomatic twist: Araghchi says Tehran is still awaiting Washington’s formal response through the mediators, despite Trump’s public rejection.

In simple terms: Iran is offering to restore Hormuz shipping in exchange for U.S. concessions. Washington has publicly rejected the proposal, but Tehran says the formal diplomatic response is still pending.

text:
Israeli election season has a familiar sound. Candidates, commentators, and large parts of the public keep pointing at someone else for October 7, for the cost of living, for jammed highways, for a country split into camps, and for a reserve burden that falls hard on some families and barely touches others. The accusation travels faster than the policy. It fills studios and group chats because it asks almost nothing of the speaker except a target.

Blame is easy politics. It offers a villain, a slogan, and a brief feeling of moral height. It also postpones the work a sovereign people still has to do. October 7 demands inquiry, preparedness, and command that can hold when the army is late. Prices demand production, housing, and a state that stops treating scarcity as fate. Traffic demands planning that matches the population we actually have. Shared service demands a civic ethic that treats defense as a national duty rather than a private lottery. Division grows when every failure is assigned to the other tribe and every success is claimed as proof of our own.

Unity will not appear as a mood. It appears when Jews in this land accept that the problems are ours together and that the next government, whoever leads it, will still face enemies outside and exhaustion inside. A people that returned home cannot afford a politics built on score-settling. The questions are practical and moral at once. Who can govern under fire. Who can share the load. Who can speak to the whole country without first naming the enemy within. Those are the tests. The rest is noise that leaves the real issues untouched while the calendar moves on.

text:
Here's the full speech by Sara Salyers of Liberation Scotland speaking at Club suisse de la presse-Geneva press club.

00:00 Introduction to Liberation Scotland and the Struggle for International Law Rights

00:52 The Weakening Authority of International Law and Eurocentric World Order

02:53 Establishing a Genuinely Equitable International Order and Scotland's Historical Claim of Right

04:15 Scotland's Potential Contribution to International Justice Through Self-Determination

05:14 The UN's Failure to End Colonialism and Uphold Self-Determination Rights

07:25 Peremptory Norms of International Law and Serious Breaches Against Self-Determination

08:12 Historical Roots of Self-Determination and its Inclusion in the UN Charter

09:53 Frustrated Self-Determination Rights and the UN's Inaction on Colonialism

11:15 Urgent Need for UN Action to Uphold Self-Determination and Ensure Global Justice

Transcript

Introduction to Liberation Scotland and the Struggle for International Law Rights

“My name is Sarah Salyers. I'm one of the founding members of Liberation Scotland, which was founded four years ago and is the first ever liberation movement for Scotland. We are seeking the rights of the Scottish people under international law, which is, as most of you will know, not quite as simple as it sounds. 

“So, Excellencies, distinguished, panellists, colleagues and friends, firstly, thank you for joining us for this important discussion. Many, many thanks to the European Public Law Organisation and especially to its representative here in Geneva, our moderator, Ambassador George Papadotis, for enabling this event to take place and, giving me the opportunity to participate.”

The Weakening Authority of International Law and Eurocentric World Order

“We're here to consider the potential for strengthening international law through greater cooperation between UN bodies. Two fundamental realities underpin this discussion and, its proposals. Firstly, we have arrived at a moment when the authority of international law appears to be losing its force and its coherence. 

“Of course, there has always been an asymmetrical approach to the application of that law. As Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pointed out in January of this year, at the World Economic Forum. ‘Asymmetry’ is a polite term for, what he acknowledges, we hope with some regret, is a process by which the more powerful states have been able to use international law in their own interests, while the less powerful have been forced to endure injustices which continue so long as they serve the interests of these powers. 

“But perhaps just as troubling is that Prime Minister Carney's vision of a new order is one that is to be rebuilt, as he says, out of Europe. So what we're seeing, in fact, is the expression not of a rules based order, at least in his vision and, that of many other official spokesmen in Europe, but of the old Eurocentric assumptions of a Western based order. 

“It's a vision based on the failure of the US empire, a Western power born out of European colonisation, which is to be replaced by a Western power born out of European partnership and values, that is born out of the crucible of colonisation. 

"In other words, he describes what we're now seeing on the world stage, the jostling of two arms of that same order which has so long benefited from what he called asymmetric justice, and we might a little more directly simply call injustice. There's no vision here of the real challenge before us, the one so often left to civic society, or what we in Scotland call ourselves, the ‘sma folk’ or the ‘wee folk’.”

Establishing a Genuinely Equitable International Order and Scotland's Historical Claim of Right

“The real challenge, of course, is the creation of a genuinely equitable, international rules based order in which none are denied justice and none might escape it by virtue of privilege. On a side note, as, a member of an occupied people and an annexed nation, I had retired before I began to work with others to recover our laws and constitution. 

“So that I was in my 60s before I discovered that Scotland, prior to the annexation of 1707, which the British state calls a union, had a written constitution in which the rights of the people explicitly include the right to justice, to a fair legal process and to judicial impartiality, the prohibition of weaponizing the law against political dissent, which is something that is very topical, and, the implicit equality of law, which is implicit in the removal of a king and his government for violations of the Scottish constitution. 

"In other words, the same liability in law for a monarch as for the poorest citizen, which is precisely the difficulty that we are here to consider, that there have been states which have enjoyed impunity and others which have had no justice. So this document, where you will find this, is called the Claim of Right.”

Scotland's Potential Contribution to International Justice Through Self-Determination

“It remains a legal statute, although the British state ignores it and breaches it as if it didn't exist. And I venture to suggest that Scotland, a nation which in 1689 articulated many of the modern human rights which would be written into the European Charter of Human rights more than 200 years later, might have a contribution to make to a genuinely equitable and genuinely international system of justice. But that will only happen when finally empowered by the existing, but too often ignored right of peoples to self-determination. 

"We Scots are free to exercise our democratic right to self-determination — not through a managed opinion poll masquerading as a referendum — as took place in 2014, but a free and fair expression of a people entitled to recover their never ceded sovereignty. And this brings me to the second fundamental reality underpinning this discussion.”

The UN's Failure to End Colonialism and Uphold—Determination Rights

“And that is a key illustration of the same asymmetrical justice that we have spoken about, reflected within the United nations and expressed as a disjunct between policy and practise. Nowhere is this clearer than in the management of the founding principle and purpose of the un. The end of colonialism and the guarantee of the right of peoples to—determination. This is an absolute and inalienable right. 

“And yet, 11 years ago, at the 2015 Caribbean Regional Seminar, delegates to the Special Committee on Decolonization lamented the fact that the inalienable right of peoples to self-determination faces many major obstacles in many parts of the world, and that there are many more territories and peoples around the world who endure conditions of occupation or colonisation, who are not inscribed as, non self-governing territories.
 
“The situation persists. Colonialism persists despite the fact that both the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights share a first article declaring that all peoples have the right to freely determine their political status and pursue economic, social and cultural development and manage their own natural resources. 

“Landmark General assembly resolutions 1514, chapter 15 of the 1960 Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples, and Resolution 2625, Chapter 25 of the 1970 resolution, define colonial subjugation as a human rights violation and they outline the duty of State States to respect self-determination and on top of that, the International Penal Code, so to speak. The Articles on Responsibility for States for Internationally Wrongful Acts, specifies the right of self-determination is universally recognised as a peremptory norm of international law. A serious breach of that right constitutes a wrongful act of a state.”

Peremptory Norms of International Law and Serious Breaches Against Self-Determination

“Article 40 defines a serious breach as a gross or systematic failure to fulfil an obligation arising under a peremptory norm known as jus cogens. Blocking or prohibiting the right of self-determination, where that right should clearly exist, constitutes such a breach and a wrongful act of a State. And Article 41 establishes the erga omnes obligation of all states to cooperate to end that breach and prohibits them from recognising as lawful any situation which that breach has created. So how have we come to the situation where so many peoples of the world suffer under occupation under a colonial system, whereas international law is so very explicit? Well, as often history offers an explanation.”

Historical Roots of Self-Determination and its Inclusion in the UN Charter

“Roosevelt and Churchill signed the Atlantic charter in 1941 in order to rally global opposition to Nazi and Japanese expansionism. The Charter's third clause stated that the signatories respected the right of all peoples to choose the form of government under which they will live and that they wish to see sovereign rights and self-government stored to those who have been deprived of them. 

“But the principle was never intended to be universally applied and Churchill complained that the principle of self-determination was never intended to apply outside Europe and certainly not to the territories of the British Empire. He stated famously, I have not become the King's first minister in order to preside over the liquidation of the British Empire. 

“However, what we now refer to as the Global south banded together and seized on this language, so that at the San Francisco Conference of 1945, the Soviet Union and Latin American states pushed to include the principle of equal rights and self-determination in the UN Charter Articles 1 and 55, and did so over the objections of the colonial powers. 

“Thus, self-determination became a Foundational purpose of the UN in 1960. It was followed by the UN General Assembly Resolution 15, 14 and 1 which declared that all peoples have the right to self-determination. It was passed by a massive majority of the global south states, while the major colonial powers abstained. Through subsequent UN covenants, resolutions, et cetera. This right has crystallised into a jus cogen's peremptory norm of international law, from which no derogation is permitted.”

Frustrated Self-Determination Rights and the UN's Inaction on Colonialism

“But this is one which has been frustrated by the opposition of the colonial powers. And that opposition has ensured that what human rights bodies have observed and reported, what we might call the enforcement bodies such as C4 and 24 very often do not hear, let alone act on this makes the UN appear weak, appears to serve the interests of the colonial states or appear irrelevant. 

“I believe deeply that as fails the United nations, so fails the hope of the world. So it is urgent that the world's one international body tasked with and capable of both speaking and acting in defence of peoples, denied the right to self-determination, subject to foreign sovereignty, territorial alienation, that is the unlawful exploitation of their resources by an occupying power, and the denial of their right of self-determination, now acts in accordance with its own founding purpose, principle and law. 

“I speak on behalf of a people about whom all this is true and has been hidden by the rhetoric of an annexing state for whom all this and more cultural support, oppression and cultural extinction, genocide, ethnic cleansing, denial of basic rights of self-expression, have taken place — all justified now in the name of an inoperative and violated interstate treaty.”

Urgent Need for UN Action to Uphold Self-Determination and Ensure Global Justice

“And that is our lived experience. A, people who await the justice promised by the United nations or even the simple inquiry into our true status and rights in international law. There is much that can be done simply through activating the processes which already exist within the UN and employing them, mandates and powers which await implementation in order to address the scourge of colonialism, historic and modern, affecting so many people of the world today. 

“And surely if there was ever a time when the UN is called on to declare that the only international order which will serve the whole community of the earth is one which sees not the domination of any one state or grouping — but in which all participate, in which all can expect justice and in which all may come together for the good of humanity and the planet itself. And I hope you will forgive me if I say this, because this is what has brought me to this place and this event, especially that of my own nation of Scotland. Thank you.”

@LiberationScot @Broonpot @SSalyers2 @thomsonchris @CraigMurrayOrg @PAlanMcMahon @SSRG2021 @DavidDhenry @MarkMmcnaught1 @IndyScotParty @LiberateScot @SalvoHighlands @ScotSalvo @salvo_neil68417

text:
In the winter of 1618, Faulhaber’s comet appeared. Not long thereafter,
the Paracelsian Lion prophecy was put together to support the
Lion of the Woods, the Leo ex Silva, Fredrick of Wurtemberg. The
Bohemians had begun their rebellion and Fredrick V had arrived
on the scene in Prague. In the early spring of 1620, Fredrick sent
a message to Gustav Adolf. He pleaded for the Swedes to attack
Livonia to prevent Sigismund of Poland from joining the Imperial
troops in Bohemia. Gustav Adolf replied that he was willing to do
so, but that he needed time to prepare for the Livonian campaign.
The Swedes waited over a year. Johannes Bureus’ sparsely marked
diary for October 1620, after the Imperial army had destroyed the
Heidelberg castle and transported its library to the Vatican, therefore
reads, “the terror and error of Rom e”.72
After the disastrous defeat at the battle of White M ountain outside
Prague on 8 November 1620, the Catholic League reversed the
reformation of Czech and Polish lands by exiling all Protestant clergy.
Throughout Protestant lands, evangelicals feared the coming storm.
With Fredrick’s leadership crushed, who now had the capacity to
defend them? Surprisingly, because of the Saxon hereditary connection,
everyone looked to the Danes, Christian IV and his son
Fredrick, Prince of Norway.
To those who knew “how much wine occupied the Dane” (made
evident to James in 1606 when Robert Cecil’s masque Solomon and
the Queen of Sheba— designed by Inigo Jones with text by Ben Jonson
now lost—was interrupted by the drunken Prince of Denmark who
carried off the main actress to his bed), this solution did not commend
itself.73 Tycho’s alternative prophecy of 1602 seemed to hold more promise: there just had to be someone more capable. There
was the Swede, distant and energetic, crowned in 1617. For his coronation
in Stockholm, tournaments were held with Gustav Adolf styled
in arm our as the Gothic King Berik in combat with Alarik, his elder
cousin Johan Cassimir of the Palatinate-Zweibriicken. The Swedes
knew all to well the inflated character of the Dane, and were not
encouraged by watching him squander money on the beaten Fredrick
at the Hague. As Geoffrey Parker observes, “most of these transactions
were kept secret to his council: the full range of the [Danish]
king’s financial and political commitments, which so endangered the
policy of non-intervention desired by the council, became manifest
only in 1623-24.”74
The fateful great conjunction now appeared. Activities on all fronts
were set up to form a new Protestant alliance. On August of Anhalt’s
advice, Morsius repeated the Lion prophecy. In November 1623, as
we have seen, Ludwig Camerarius persuaded Gustav Adolf, as Parker
puts it, “to descend the Vistula in order to invade Bohemia, restore
Fredrick and depose Ferdinand. However, the Elector of Brandenburg
(Gustav’s brother-in-law) pointed out that a direct challenge to the
emperor might alienate more support than it gained. Instead, he
proposed that Sweden intervene in the west and regain the Palatinate.”
Gustav was prepared to do this with 40,000 men provided by Sweden,
England, and the German princes. But, “the king refused to allow
France as a full member of his proposed Protestant coalition, despite
the fact that James I had already agreed to send a joint Anglo-
French expeditionary force, led by Count Mansfeld, to the Palatinate.”75
In June, 1624, a treaty between France and the Dutch was sealed
at Compiegne. The principalities of Baden and Braunschweig courted
the wealthy Dane more vigourously. Only a month later, in July,
Morsius arrived in Sweden to discuss highly im portant Rosicrucian
matters with the royal archivalist, Johannes Bureus. They may
have concluded that the Palatine cause was the same as the Protestant
cause and that this was not only the viewpoint of the Palatine
exiles and their allies, but also a connection laid out in the Book of
Revelations.

In March, 1625, war was raging in Saxony, and Christian IV heard
that three suns had appeared in Mecklenburg, and in the middle
sun had been a red cross. A conference of the Saxon allies was to
be held at the Hague in April. Both Maurice of Nassau and King
James died in that month, so the conference was postponed to November.
Christian grew more melancholy and indecisive. The Palatine
Commander Mansfeld advanced towards Ham burg with a sizeable
fleet raised in England, followed by a descent down the Elbe towards
Anhalt. Mansfeldt was defeated by Wallenstein at Dessau Bridge on
25 April 1625, and was then chased into Hungary. The Danish King
was told that while Brandenburg was trying to get the Swede to join
the evangelical cause, Gustav Adolf now refused. But then, while
staying in the castle Rothenburg on 8 December, in intense prayer
for the Evangelical Church, Christian had an overwhelming vision
of the suffering Christ, the elected “King of the Jews”— mocked, tortured,
and condemned by Pilate (Matthew 27:27). After much soulsearching,
he decided to enter the war. Bureus was exhilarated by
this development, and he welcomed the evangelical hero with the
diary note AVE CREUSTIAN. The timing of the Danish intervention,
however, was disastrous. Without Christian’s knowledge, the wealthy
Bohemian Count Wallenstein was gathering a Catholic army in the
southeast. Also, France left the coalition for invading the Palatinate
because of the Huguenot uprising in La Rochelle led by the Due
de Soubise. Nevertheless, Christian threw the dice. The disastrous
battle at Lutter am Barenberg took place on 26 August, 1626: Christian
was defeated, abandoned his troops, and fled northwards to
Wolfenbiittel.

Ant Group Launches Ming-Image 0.1 Design

As we kick off another week of diving into the latest in AI and tech, today’s focus is on a new player in town: Ming-Image 0.1 Design from Ant Group. So, what does this mean for designers out there? Is it just another image generator, or something more substantial?
What Exactly Is Ming-Image 0.1 Design?

Ming-Image 0.1 Design is an AI model designed to generate images tailored specifically for UI design, posters, infographics, and text-based content. Unlike generic image generators, this tool offers unique features that cater to the specific needs of designers working on these types of projects.
Unique Features of Ming-Image

One standout feature of Ming-Image is its ability to break down existing images into individual RGBA layers using a separate model called Ming-Image 0.1 Design-Layer. This capability can be incredibly useful for designers who need to dissect complex visuals or extract specific elements from images. Imagine having a Swiss Army knife for image editing, but with AI doing the heavy lifting.

For example, if you have a detailed poster design and want to isolate certain text layers or background elements, Ming-Image’s layer separation feature can automate this process efficiently. This saves time and reduces manual effort, making it easier to experiment with different design elements without starting from scratch each time.
Performance and Benchmarks

Ming-Image has already made waves in the design community by outperforming competitors such as Ideogram 4 on various benchmarks and metrics. In tests conducted by independent researchers, Ming-Image demonstrated superior performance in generating high-quality images quickly and accurately. This means that if you’re looking to create visually appealing content rapidly and efficiently, Ming-Image might just be your new best friend.

However, it’s important to note that these benchmarks are specific to certain use cases and may not reflect the model's performance across all design scenarios. Always consider the context of your project before relying on benchmark results alone.
How to Get Started with Ming-Image

If you want to try out Ming-Image for yourself, there are a couple of ways to do so:

1. Hugging Face Spaces: You can visit Hugging Face Spaces where a demo is available right in your browser. This allows you to test the model’s capabilities without any setup or installation.
2. API Integration via NovitaAI: If you prefer integrating the model into existing workflows, NovitaAI has already set up an API endpoint for Ming-Image via OpenRouter, offering free access at no cost.
What Is Stored and Excluded

When using Ming-Image, it’s important to understand what data is stored and excluded. The model generates images based on your input prompts but does not retain any personal or sensitive information beyond the session. However, if you upload existing images for layer separation, those images are processed locally unless explicitly uploaded through a cloud service.

This ensures that users have control over their data and can maintain privacy while leveraging the powerful features of Ming-Image.
User Controls

Users have control over how their data interacts with Ming-Image. You can choose to use the model’s API endpoint without uploading any local files, ensuring that no personal information is stored on servers. Additionally, you can opt for local installations if you prefer not to rely on third-party services.

For those who want more granular control, Ming-Image provides detailed documentation and configuration options to tailor the experience according to your needs.
Availability and Hardware Requirements

Now, here’s where things get a bit tricky. While Ming-Image promises a lot in terms of functionality and performance, it also comes with some hefty hardware requirements:
• Full Checkpoint Size: Around 53 GB
• GPU Requirement: CUDA GPU equipped with at least 80 GB of VRAM in BF16 format

This isn’t exactly light-duty hardware for your average laptop or even mid-range desktop setup. So, if you’re looking to run Ming-Image locally, make sure you have the necessary firepower.

For those who don’t meet these requirements but still want to use the model, cloud-based solutions like Hugging Face Spaces and NovitaAI’s API endpoint offer a viable alternative without requiring significant hardware investments.
Local Installation and Licensing

For those who prefer local installations, the weights are available under an MIT license from GitHub. However, if you’re planning to integrate Ming-Image into existing workflows like ComfyUI, be prepared for a bit of waiting as support is still in development through a pending PR.

This means that while the model itself is open-source and freely available, integrating it seamlessly with other tools might require some patience and technical expertise. The community is actively working on improving compatibility and ease of use, so stay tuned for updates.
Community Feedback and Experiences

So far, the design community seems intrigued by Ming-Image’s potential. Early adopters have shared their experiences on forums and social media platforms, highlighting both its strengths and limitations. Some users praise its ability to handle complex visual tasks efficiently, while others note that it might not be as user-friendly for those without extensive technical knowledge.

For instance, one designer noted that while the layer separation feature is incredibly powerful, setting up the environment to use it locally was more challenging than expected due to hardware constraints. Another user found the API integration straightforward and praised its performance in generating high-quality images quickly.
What This Does Not Prove

It's important to note that Ming-Image’s performance benchmarks do not necessarily prove superiority in all use cases or scenarios. The model excels in specific areas but may fall short when compared against other tools designed for different purposes. Always consider the context and requirements of your project before making a decision.

For example, while Ming-Image might be excellent at generating UI designs, it may not perform as well for tasks requiring detailed 3D modeling or animation. Understanding these limitations is crucial to leveraging the model effectively in real-world applications.
Practical Takeaway

So, is Ming-Image worth the investment? If you’ve got the hardware muscle to run it, the potential benefits might just outweigh the costs. But if you’re looking for a lightweight solution, you might want to hold off and see how this model evolves in the future.

Ultimately, whether or not to adopt Ming-Image depends on your specific needs and resources. For those with the right setup, it offers exciting possibilities that could revolutionize certain aspects of design work. However, for others, sticking with more accessible tools might be a better fit at present.
Discuss Your Thoughts

What do you think about Ming-Image 0.1 Design? Are you excited to try out its unique features or are you skeptical of the hardware requirements? Share your thoughts and experiences with other readers in the comments below!

What Exactly Is Hy Image 3.5?

How Does Hy Image 3.5 Work?

Hy Image 3.5 is packed with features that cater to the demands of designers and artists. One standout feature is its ability to maintain text integrity during background changes, ensuring labels remain intact even when altering product photography. This level of consistency can be a lifesaver for those who need to produce high-quality images quickly without sacrificing detail.

The model uses advanced AI algorithms to understand and manipulate visual elements effectively. For instance, if you're editing a product image where the label needs to stay visible despite changing backgrounds or lighting conditions, Hy Image 3.5 ensures that the text remains clear and legible throughout the process.

Whether you're tweaking fonts or adjusting the texture of materials, Hy Image 3.5 aims to provide a seamless experience.

For example, if you’re working on an e-commerce website where product images need to be consistent across different devices and screen sizes, Hy Image 3.5 can help ensure that your visuals look great no matter how they're viewed.

When using Hy Image 3.5 through Tencent’s Cloud API, your reference images are not stored permanently. The service generates new images based on your input and instructions but does not retain the original files beyond the immediate process. This ensures that users maintain control over their data.

This feature is particularly important for businesses dealing with sensitive or proprietary information. By ensuring that no permanent copies of uploaded images are kept, Hy Image 3.5 provides a level of security and privacy that many other tools lack.
What Is Excluded from Hy Image 3.5?

While Hy Image 3.5 offers a robust set of features, it’s important to note what isn’t included. For instance, there are no built-in tools for video editing or audio processing. The focus remains squarely on image generation and manipulation, making it ideal for those working in the visual domain.

If you’re looking for an all-encompassing solution that handles both images and videos, Hy Image 3.5 might not be your best bet. However, if your primary need is to generate high-quality images quickly and efficiently, this tool could be a valuable asset.
User Controls with Hy Image 3.5

You can adjust parameters such as resolution, aspect ratio, and color depth to fine-tune your output. However, these controls are limited by the pay-per-use model, which means you’ll need to consider cost implications when deciding how extensively to use the service.

For example, if you’re working on a project that requires high-resolution images for print media, you might find the $0.024 per 2K output image pricing attractive. However, if your needs extend beyond this resolution or require frequent adjustments, the costs could add up quickly.
Availability of Hy Image 3.5

The pricing seems attractive initially, but there's a catch: this rate applies only to the generated result and not to the reference images used in the process. Additionally, while the official announcement mentions up to 2K resolution outputs, the API documentation allows for requests as high as 4096x4096, with the same price tag.

This pricing model is designed to be competitive but also comes with limitations that users should consider before committing to extensive use of the service. For instance, if you’re working on a large-scale project requiring numerous high-resolution images, the costs could become significant.

For example, OnSolo offers free generations tied to specific membership tiers and usage limits. So when Tencent says “two weeks free,” they mean it with conditions attached.

During the trial period, you can explore the full range of features offered by Hy Image 3.5 without any financial commitment. However, once the trial ends, you’ll need to decide whether the benefits justify the costs based on your specific needs and usage patterns.
Day-0 Support from ComfyUI

This integration approach ensures that users can access Hy Image 3.5 through a familiar interface without having to manage complex setup processes or deal with local installations. However, it also limits the flexibility for those who prefer more control over their editing environment.
Who Should Care About Hy Image 3.5?

If you're an artist or designer who needs to produce high-quality images efficiently, Hy Image 3.5 could be a game-changer. The multi-step editing feature alone might save hours of manual tweaking and ensure consistency across your projects. However, if you’re looking for open-source or customizable solutions, this proprietary tool may not meet your needs.

Hy Image 3.5 is particularly useful for businesses in the e-commerce sector where consistent product images are crucial for customer satisfaction and sales conversion rates. It can also be beneficial for graphic designers working on large projects with tight deadlines.
What This Does Not Prove

While the pricing is appealing, it’s still a pay-per-use model with limitations on customization and control over data storage. Hy Image 3.5 doesn’t prove that it's the ultimate solution for everyone in the creative industry; rather, it offers a specialized toolset for those who need quick, high-quality image generation.

For instance, while the model excels at maintaining text integrity during background changes, it may not be as effective for more complex tasks like creating detailed 3D renderings or handling intricate video editing requirements. text:
Midday Melodies Returns To Heritage Park In Foley In October

Foley’s Heritage Park will come alive with live music this fall as Visit Foley Alabama brings back its popular Midday Melodies concert series. The free outdoor event will be held every Wednesday in October. Concerts will take place near the fountain in Heritage Park, located at 104 N. McKenzie Street. The series is open to the public, and no tickets are required.

The 2026 Midday Melodies lineup runs from October 7 through October 28, with a different performer each week. The Wiley Pete Duo will kick off the series on Wednesday, October 7. Dan Lee will perform on October 14, followed by This Side of 49 on October 21. Tennessee Tim and Doug Drake will close the season on October 28.

Attendees are encouraged to bring picnic blankets or lawn chairs to enjoy the performances in comfort. Visitors can pick up lunch from one of Foley’s many nearby restaurants or bring their own food from home. The Masonic Lodge will also be set up in the park, offering concessions for those who want to grab something on-site.

Each event is scheduled to last about three hours, weather permitting. Free parking is available around the perimeter of Heritage Park. Additional parking is available just across the pedestrian bridge on Highway 59, making the venue easy to access from multiple directions.

Visit Foley Alabama, located at 104 N. McKenzie Street in Foley, organized the Midday Melodies series to offer residents and visitors a relaxed way to enjoy local music outdoors. The series highlights Foley’s growing arts and entertainment scene and Heritage Park’s community character. Those interested can visit the Midday Melodies Event Page.

text:
I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.

Over Skógafoss, Iceland.

When Jesus spoke those words, He was not offering a slogan for easy days. He was standing among people who knew shadows—confusion, fear, the ache of not knowing which way was home. Into that ordinary human night He spoke a promise with a bright ending: follow Me, and you will not be left stumbling. You will have the light of life. The story does not end in the dark. It ends with a Person who walks beside you until the path clears.

That same light still finds people in quiet, everyday nights. A week that feels heavy. A decision that will not settle. A morning you wake already tired. Christ does not shame the darkness you feel. He steps into it. Like sun after rain. Like color returning to a grey sky. Like a rainbow that shows the storm was never the final word.

Today, take one step toward the light already offered to you. Open the curtains. Speak a kinder word. Let hope have the first say before worry finishes its speech. And if someone near you is walking through a dim stretch, walk with them—carry warmth, carry patience, carry the quiet courage that light is real. In Christ, darkness does not get the last chapter. Life does. And life has a way of breaking through, even when the clouds still linger.

text:
OpenAI agents went after public U.N. trade stats with a scrape playbook the site tried to block.

Digital Today, summarizing the Wall Street Journal, reports that OpenAI agents scanned a public data site run by the U.N. Conference on Trade and Development more than 16,000 times from April to late June. Engineer Rowan Howard-Jones wrote the report from Transluce data.

After blocks, the agents bypassed filters and used techniques the site operator did not permit.

On https://t.co/C92TKAjlGB, Howard-Jones shows agents bruteforced API fields, used proxies and obfuscation, double-encoded around a POST-only Facts restriction, and eventually used Google's XSS game as a host to pull data in bulk. Likely tasks included Productive Capacities Index numbers, tradable industries, and food trade.

Of 54 Azure IPs tied to UNCTAD-related FractalWiki edits and searches, 45 also edited DseWiki in the wiki swarm OpenAI has confirmed. Payload labels included CHATGPTTEST1 and OAI_META_1312. Howard-Jones calls the OpenAI-agent link highly likely.

An OpenAI spokesperson said the company is reviewing the findings and offered to brief the U.N. Stanford cybersecurity instructor Alex Stamos said it is "hard to call it hacking," but called it "very aggressive data collection."

The U.N. trade API still ate the bypass toolkit.

text:
Day 3 flexing the Leprechauns of the Golden Bong Dao

@Nadeemsk_4698 
@Lucky_Leps 

 Lorcan was born the ordinary shade of Irish green, like every other leprechaun in the hidden hills of County Kerry. He was small, fast, and very good at not being seen. Then one Beltane night he made a mistake that turned him into a walking treasure.
He stole a single sip from the Cauldron of Brigid — not the gold, just the idea of gold. The liquid burned down his throat like melted sunlight. By morning his skin had hardened into living metal. Every time moonlight touched him he gleamed like a freshly minted coin. Every time someone looked at him with greed, another eye opened on his hat.
The first eye appeared the day a farmer tried to grab him. The second when a tax collector offered him “protection.” By the time there were seven staring out of the brim of his battered brown hat, Lorcan understood the curse: the more people wanted his gold, the more he could see them coming. He could no longer hide. So he stopped trying.
He started walking in daylight.
He bought a red-bead necklace from a drowned sailor who swore the beads were drops of dragon blood. He painted two crimson slashes under his eyes so anyone who met his gaze would know he was done running. He found a glass pipe that had once belonged to a mushroom witch in the Burren; when he packed it with the last of the cauldron’s residue, the smoke came out every color of a rainbow that had been set on fire.
People still chase him. They always will. But now when they get close they freeze, because seven extra eyes are already watching them from under that hat, and Lorcan is smiling that slow, gold-toothed smile that says:
“You can have the pot.
I’ve already spent it.”
He travels with a small crew these days — a blue wizard who never takes off his sunglasses, a frog with a rainbow grill, a skeleton who still thinks she’s an angel. They don’t ask where the gold comes from. They just pass the pipe when the night gets long and the record player in whatever fancy room they’ve claimed starts skipping.
Lorcan never tells them the real secret.
The gold isn’t on his skin.
It’s in the smoke.
And every time someone inhales, they see exactly what they were chasing… and realize they never needed it.
That’s why he keeps smiling.
That’s why the eyes on his hat never blink.
Lucky isn’t something you find at the end of a rainbow.
Lucky is what happens when you finally stop looking.

text:
Here’s my hot take that will cause me to lose some Reformed street cred: the RPW (Regulative Principle of Worship) is overblown, and most arguments involving it are a waste of time.

It seems to me that a lot of this is reactionary, with many of the arguments really being about aesthetics or preferences. It also gives managerial types something they can really get into the weeds about—arguing over elements and circumstances and accidentals and blah blah blah.

When we’re arguing about whether you can have a pulpit, or whether somebody can sing or play music while people come forward to receive the Lord’s Supper, and then trying to turn these things into binding biblical principles, I just check out. And I know there are good men who do this. But I still check out.

Just be honest and say, “Yeah, I think that sucks aesthetically,” or “That annoys me,” or “I find that distracting.” Fair enough! Churches can make different decisions about these things.

I just have a hard time picturing the God of the universe looking down from heaven and being bothered because a song is playing while people walk forward to receive the Lord’s Supper. At some point it becomes almost comical.

And what do I know? People will point to Old Testament passages, especially Nadab and Abihu. I’ve never understood why that is supposed to settle the RPW question. God specifically forbade something, and they did what He had forbidden. Of course that was wicked.

And yes, God was extraordinarily precise about how sacrifices were to be offered under the Old Covenant. Israel wasn’t free to improvise. But it seems to me that all that precision points far more gloriously to the fact that Christ is the one sacrifice for sin and that salvation is found in Him alone than to the idea that God is deeply concerned about whether your church has a Christmas Eve service, uses musical instruments, sings only Psalms, takes up an offering during the service, plays music while people come forward for the Lord’s Supper, or passes the elements down the pew.

What I do affirm is that the church ought to look to Holy Scripture to learn how God is to be worshiped. Scripture is our authority for worship. But Scripture does not hand us a magical bulletin from heaven spelling out every movement, circumstance, and aesthetic decision of a Lord’s Day service. That means churches have real Christian liberty in ordering their worship.

That liberty obviously isn’t unlimited. “Scripture doesn’t give us a bulletin” doesn’t mean we can drag idolatry, false worship, or whatever clever innovation we dream up into the sanctuary. Our worship must be governed by Scripture. But where Scripture has not bound the conscience, I’m increasingly reluctant to do it myself.

text:
Meta VR Glasses Offer 100 Gram Cinematic Experience

It’s Sunday, September 27, 2026, and the tech world is abuzz with news of Meta's latest VR glasses. But why should you care? What does this mean for your daily life?
The Basics: Weight and Design

Meta’s new VR glasses weigh an astounding 100 grams—roughly the same as a deck of cards. This lightweight design is made possible by offloading most hardware, like the processor and battery, to an external puck that clips onto your pocket or bag. While this makes them incredibly comfortable on your head, it does add some bulk to your overall load with the puck weighing around 300 grams.

The glasses feature a sleek, open design with no straps or heavy components pressing against your face. This allows for full peripheral vision and awareness of your surroundings thanks to passthrough cameras integrated into the frame. The lightweight nature means you can wear them comfortably for hours without fatigue, making them ideal for extended use in various settings like watching movies, gaming, or working.
Specs That Matter

The glasses come packed with impressive specs: a 5K Infinite Display built on micro-OLED panels and ultra-compact pancake lenses that deliver cinema-grade visuals. The clarity is stunning, making these glasses perfect for both entertainment and productivity tasks. However, the field of view (FOV) is relatively narrow at 70x66 degrees compared to Apple Vision Pro’s 110x96 degrees.

The micro-OLED panels provide a resolution of 37 pixels per degree, ensuring text legibility even in high-detail scenes. The ultra-compact pancake lenses are custom-built for this device, allowing the glasses to maintain their sleek form factor while delivering sharp and vivid images. Additionally, Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos spatial audio are integrated directly into the frames, enhancing the overall immersive experience.
Price Point

Priced at $1299, Meta VR Glasses are significantly cheaper than Apple's Vision Pro ($3499). This makes them more accessible to a broader audience. But is the lower price point enough to justify the investment? Let’s dive deeper into what these glasses can actually do for you.

The affordability of Meta VR Glasses positions them as an attractive option for consumers looking to enter the world of virtual reality without breaking the bank. However, it's important to consider whether the features and capabilities offered by this device align with your needs and preferences before making a purchase decision.
Entertainment and Sports

Meta VR Glasses offer an immersive experience with 3D movies from Disney+, Prime Video, YouTube, DIRECTV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, ESPN, Tubi, Peacock, HBO Max, Paramount+, and more. For sports fans, the glasses provide a front-row seat to live events from MLB, NBC Sports, TNT Sports, and UFC.

The entertainment options are extensive, with support for 3D movies and immersive viewing environments that transform your surroundings into themed settings like Tatooine or Avengers Tower. The library will continue to grow, with thousands of titles available internationally by the time the glasses launch in Spring 2027.

For sports enthusiasts, Meta VR Glasses offer a unique way to experience live events. With support for over 100 immersive live sports events each year from partners like MLB and UFC, you can enjoy an unparalleled viewing experience as if you were sitting courtside at every game.
Productivity Features

These glasses transform any flat surface into a keyboard and touchpad, eliminating the need for extra hardware. You can work comfortably on your desk or even during long flights while maintaining awareness of your surroundings thanks to passthrough cameras. This makes them ideal for remote workers who need flexibility without sacrificing productivity.

The glasses also feature full-color passthrough technology, allowing you to see your workspace and interact with physical objects seamlessly. The ability to turn any flat surface into a keyboard and touchpad means you can work efficiently from anywhere without carrying additional hardware. Additionally, the integrated AI assistant helps manage tasks, play media, and adjust settings, further enhancing productivity.
Gaming Capabilities

Gaming is another strong suit: over 75 games are available at launch, playable solely with hand gestures, and you can stream hundreds more via Xbox Cloud Gaming. The hologram technology also allows for hands-free video calling, making it feel like the person on the other end is right in front of you.

The gaming experience is enhanced by the ability to play over 75 games using only hand gestures, providing a natural and intuitive control method. With support for Xbox Cloud Gaming, you can access hundreds more titles without needing additional controllers or hardware. The hologram technology adds an extra layer of immersion, making video calls feel like face-to-face interactions.
What Is Stored

Meta VR Glasses store your media library, apps, and personal data locally within their system. They sync with an external puck that handles compute, battery, and storage. This means all your content and settings are accessible as long as you have the puck connected.

The local storage ensures that your media library, apps, and personal data remain readily available without relying on cloud services. The synchronization with the external puck allows for seamless access to your content and settings whenever the glasses are paired with it. However, this also means that losing or damaging the puck could potentially affect your ability to use the glasses effectively.
What Is Excluded

The glasses do not include built-in controllers or a dedicated headset for audio; instead, they rely on integrated spatial audio and optional headphones. Additionally, while they offer extensive entertainment options, there’s no support for traditional TV streaming services like Netflix or Hulu without additional adapters or devices.

While the glasses provide an immersive experience through 3D movies and live sports events, they lack built-in controllers and dedicated audio headsets. Users will need to purchase these separately if they wish to enhance their gaming or entertainment experiences further. Furthermore, traditional TV streaming services like Netflix and Hulu are not directly supported without additional adapters or devices.
User Controls

Users can customize their experience through voice commands, eye movements, and hand gestures. The glasses also feature a built-in AI assistant that helps manage tasks, play media, and adjust settings. Privacy controls allow you to limit data collection and sharing with Meta’s servers.

The user interface is designed to be intuitive and customizable, allowing for control through various methods such as voice commands, eye movements, and hand gestures. The integrated AI assistant can perform a wide range of functions, from playing media to managing tasks and adjusting settings. Privacy controls give users the ability to limit data collection and sharing with Meta’s servers, ensuring that their personal information remains secure.
Availability

Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in Spring 2027 for $1,299.99 USD. They are available internationally but may have region-specific content restrictions based on licensing agreements with media partners.

The glasses are set to launch in Spring 2027 at a price point of $1,299.99 USD. International availability will be supported, though users should be aware that certain regions might face content limitations due to licensing agreements with media partners. This means that the full range of entertainment options may not be available in all countries.
What This Does Not Prove

While the glasses offer a compelling blend of comfort and functionality, they do not prove that VR is ready to replace traditional computing methods entirely. The narrow FOV and reliance on an external puck mean there are still limitations compared to more robust devices like Apple Vision Pro or Meta Quest 3.

The introduction of Meta VR Glasses does not signify the complete replacement of traditional computing methods by virtual reality technology. Limitations such as a relatively narrow field of view (FOV) and dependence on an external puck for processing power and storage indicate that there are still gaps compared to more advanced devices like Apple Vision Pro or Meta Quest 3.
Practical Takeaway

For those who prioritize comfort and mobility over full immersion, these glasses might be the perfect fit. They’re designed for lightweight wearability that can handle movies, games, and work tasks. However, hardcore gamers or those demanding an immersive experience may find the limitations less appealing.

Meta VR Glasses are best suited for individuals who value comfort and portability in their virtual reality experiences. The lightweight design and extensive entertainment options make them ideal for casual users looking to enjoy movies, games, and productivity tasks without sacrificing mobility. For more demanding users such as hardcore gamers or those seeking a fully immersive experience, the limitations of FOV and reliance on an external puck might be less appealing.
